nodes.name: Arctic willow
nodes.desc: A dwarf willow hugging the ground on tundra. Willows are the most commonly eaten plant for muskoxen in winter.

nodes.name: Mountain avens
nodes.desc: A low, mat-forming tundra wildflower that is one of the well-recorded plants of the coast.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Grass-like plants of wet tundra. Muskoxen and barnacle geese graze sedges and grasses.

nodes.name: Arctic bell-heather
nodes.desc: A small evergreen heath shrub of tundra. GloBI records Arctic hares feeding on it.

nodes.name: Sea-ice algae
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that grow in and under sea ice, the base of the marine food chain here.

nodes.name: Muskox
nodes.desc: The park holds a large share of the world population. It eats grasses, sedges and willows, and Arctic wolves are its main predator.

nodes.name: Collared lemming
nodes.desc: A small tundra rodent that turns white in winter. Its numbers rise and fall in cycles, which drive its predators.

nodes.name: Arctic hare
nodes.desc: A large hare of the tundra that browses low plants such as heather and willow.

nodes.name: Barnacle goose
nodes.desc: A summer breeding visitor that grazes sedges and grasses. It is one of the most recorded birds here.

nodes.name: Arctic copepod
nodes.desc: A tiny crustacean of Arctic seas that feeds on ice algae and phytoplankton and feeds fish.

nodes.name: Arctic fox
nodes.desc: Hunts lemmings, hares and birds, and scavenges carcasses left by polar bears and wolves.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small weasel listed among the park's land mammals. It preys on lemmings and other small animals.

nodes.name: Long-tailed jaeger
nodes.desc: A tundra-nesting seabird that hunts lemmings and small birds in summer.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A year-round resident that scavenges carcasses and other leftovers.

nodes.name: Polar cod
nodes.desc: A small fish living near sea ice that feeds on copepods and is prey for seals.

nodes.name: Ringed seal
nodes.desc: The most common prey of polar bears, and a seal that depends on sea ice. It eats fish and crustaceans.

nodes.name: Arctic wolf
nodes.desc: A small but important population lives here. Wolves are the main predator of muskoxen and also take hares and birds.

nodes.name: Polar bear
nodes.desc: Hunts mainly ringed seals from the sea ice. Its kills feed foxes and ravens.

nodes.name: Midnight sun
nodes.desc: Long summer daylight gives a short, intense growing season on the tundra; winter is dark.

nodes.name: Tundra soil
nodes.desc: Thin, cold soils over permafrost where nutrients are released slowly.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria that break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients slowly in the cold.

nodes.name: Sea ice
nodes.desc: Frozen sea water that hosts ice algae and is the hunting platform of polar bears.
